- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day forecast, especially after sharp spikes or dips.
- Overestimates in the middle of the forecast horizon, particularly when recent history shows volatility or recovery.
- Tends to overshoot after a price spike, then corrects too slowly — lagging mean reversion.
- Mean reversion bias: model assumes prices return to historical mean too quickly, missing longer-term trends.
- Forecasts are overly sensitive to recent low values, leading to premature “bottoming” signals.
- Underestimates upward momentum in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, especially when true prices show strong upward drift.
- Overconfident in short-term volatility, underestimating sustained upward trends in the last 10–15 days.
- Model exhibits “anchoring” bias — fails to adjust for recent high prices when forecasting future values.
